$comment: Generated by scripts/gen-contract.mjs from contract/*.schema.json and contract/api/*.schema.json. Do not edit.

AddSummary.description: midstudy-add's last stdout line on success (contract §3.1), which the server reads after a library job. v1 names the engine rescale for --rescale and gives paths as it was given --library (relative or absolute); a path is null when the item has no such file.

Align.description: rooms/<room>/align.json (contract §4.3 align-room, §4.9): the pose solver's last answer for a room's photos, written atomically by `midstudy-calib align-room` (never by the server). Poses and scales are relative to the first scene folder the command was given (pose {0, 0, 0}, scale 1), in the §4.9 convention. `align-room` prints the same object plus "ok": true as its last stdout line. Keys not listed here are allowed at the top level for diagnostics; readers ignore them.

solver.description: Which solver answered: manhattan (the no-ML fallback), the chosen learned solver's name (e.g. vggt, mast3r, solv3r; Gate A, docs/ROOMS.md §5), truth (the golden room fixtures' mock answers), none (nothing could be placed: the mock without a match, or every solver failed).

created.description: When the answer was written, ISO-8601 UTC.

loop_residual_cm.description: How far the poses disagree around closed loops of overlapping photos (cm), or null when there is no loop (fewer than three placed photos, or a chain).

members.description: Every scene folder given, in the order given. members[0] is the frame: pose {0, 0, 0}, scale 1, confidence 1, residual_cm null.

unplaced.description: The scenes of the members whose pose is null, in member order (never members[0]).

AlignAccepted.description: 202 of POST /api/rooms/<room>/align (contract §4.9 Align): the queued job.

AlignJob.description: An align job (contract §4.9 Align): runs `align-room` on the calibration queue. GET /api/rooms/jobs/<id>, inside the jobs list and the 202 of POST /api/rooms/<room>/align. In memory: a restart forgets them.

message.description: A human-readable status line; a failed job's is the tool's error sentence.

waiting_for.description: While queued: the member scenes it waits for (calibration pending or running); empty otherwise.

align.description: The answer (align.json) once done, else null.

AlignMember.description: One photo's answer. pose and scale are both null (unplaced) or both set.

scene.description: The scene folder's name (the last path segment of its argument).

photo_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the scene's photo.jpg as it was read (lowercase hex): an answer for a photo since replaced is stale.

pose.description: Relative to members[0], or null when the solver couldn't place this photo.

scale.description: This photo's scale relative to members[0] (multiplies its camera's height_m), or null when unplaced.

confidence.description: 0–1: how sure the solver is of this pose (0 when unplaced). The planner flags a placed photo below 0.5.

residual_cm.description: The median distance between this photo's depth points and the other placed photos' where they overlap, after alignment (cm); null for members[0], when unplaced, or when it overlaps no other placed photo.

AlignRequest.description: POST /api/rooms/<room>/align (contract §4.9 Align): no body, or this object. 409 while an align job for the room is queued or running, or when fewer than two members have a photo.jpg or a calibration queued or running (a just-uploaded photo counts; the job waits for it).

overwrite_manual.description: Also replace the poses of manual members with the answer (default false: they keep theirs).

AlignStatus.description: pending while an align job is queued (also while it waits for members to calibrate), running while it runs; else done when align.json exists and the last align job (if any since the server started) succeeded; failed when the last one failed; none when the room was never aligned (no align.json, no job).

ApiError.description: Every /api error answer (contract §2.1): one sentence. Routes with richer errors name their own schema in routes.json (402: spend-refused, product: product-error).

Calib.description: Written by `midstudy-calib fit` (and `run`). `midstudy-calib run` prints the same object plus "ok": true as its last stdout line. Keys not listed here are allowed for diagnostics; readers ignore them.

ok.description: Only on the stdout line of `run` / `fit`, never in the file.

source.description: moge-2: MoGe fitted the camera; exif: fallback with the FOV from the EXIF focal length; default: fallback with FOV 55; truth: golden scenes only (fixtures/scenes).

model.description: The MoGe weights used, e.g. Ruicheng/moge-2-vitl-normal; null when MoGe didn't run.

principal.description: Principal point as a fraction of width and height. Recorded, but v1 always renders with the image center.

inlier_ratio.description: Share of the image's pixels that lie on the fitted floor plane.

rmse_m.description: RMS distance of the inliers to the plane, meters.

depth.description: depth.png next to calib.json: 16-bit grayscale, mm along the camera's view axis, 0 = no occluder (floor within 4 cm of the plane, sky, unknown). Null when there is no depth (fallbacks, --no-depth).

exif.description: What the upload's EXIF said, read from source.<ext> (photo.jpg has no metadata). Null without EXIF.

fov_y_deg.description: Vertical FOV from focal_35mm (native 4:3 frame, then the crop that keeps the width).

fov_source.description: Whose FOV the camera uses: the photo's EXIF focal length (when it agrees with MoGe's within 8 degrees; MoGe's scale is then corrected by the focal ratio, contract §4.3 Fit) or MoGe's own. Absent on mock, fallback and truth calibrations.

moge.description: MoGe-2's own estimates and timings (fov_x_deg, fov_y_deg, input, load_s, infer_s, floor_fit_s) and, with fov_source exif, the correction: height_m (MoGe's own), scale (tan(fov_moge/2) / tan(fov_exif/2)), depth_scale.

fov_disagreement.description: Present when MoGe's and the EXIF vertical FOV differ by more than 8 degrees.

CalibCliAlignRoom.description: `align-room` (contract §4.3, §4.9): align.json's contents (align.schema.json) plus "ok": true; the same object the command wrote to <room-dir>/align.json.

CalibCliError.description: Any command that failed: exit 1 (one-shot), the same sentence as the last stderr line after `midstudy-calib: `.

error.description: One sentence the server shows as it is.

CalibCliId.description: Worker responses only: the request's id (null when the request had no usable id).

CalibCliLightNone.description: `light` found too little to go on and wrote nothing.

CalibCliRequest.description: One line on the worker's stdin.

args.description: The one-shot command's arguments after its name, as an argument list.

CalibrateAccepted.description: 202 of POST /api/scenes/<name>/calibrate (contract §4.4): fit on photo.jpg, or run on source.<ext> when photo.jpg is missing. 409 while one is queued or running for that scene.

message.description: A human-readable status line; a failed job's is the tool's error sentence.

calib.description: The result (without exif.make, exif.model) once done, else null.

Camera.description: The camera block (contract §4.1). Ranges are clamped by every writer.

CameraPatch.description: Any of the camera block's keys, merged into the camera in use, then clamped (§4.1).

Dims.description: Width (X), depth (Z) and height (Y) in centimeters.

DimsCandidate.description: One size reading, in cm rounded to 0.1.

h.description: Null when the page has no height (never for a rug: its thickness, 1 cm when the page has none). v1 reads a rug's thickness from 0.1 cm.

unit_note.description: How it was converted when the page's unit wasn't cm.

quote.description: The text, structured value or feed text the numbers came from.

JpegDataUri.description: A JPEG as a base64 data URI (contract §2.6). The server stores and sends it without its metadata.

Layout.description: A scene's or a room's furniture placement. Every layout belongs to exactly one scene (scene_name) or exactly one room (room_name, contract §4.9), never both, never neither. The camera is the scene's (scene.json), not the layout's; a room layout's positions and rotations are in the room frame.

title.description: The name as the user typed it ("Phone A"), shown instead of the slug; optional.

scene_name.description: The scene this layout belongs to (its folder name, e.g. scene-20261104-201500). The server sets it from ?scene=. Exactly one of scene_name and room_name.

room_name.description: The room this layout belongs to (contract §4.9; its folder name, e.g. room-20261106-101500). The server sets it from ?room=. Exactly one of scene_name and room_name.

library.description: Library URL the layout was made with.

updated.description: Set by the server on PUT, ISO-8601 UTC.

LayoutDeleted.description: DELETE /api/layouts/<layout>?scene=<name> or ?room=<room> (contract §2.7, §4.9): the file moved to layouts/<scene>/.trash/<layout>-<UTC stamp>.json (a room's: layouts/@<room>/.trash/…). v1 also names the layout and scene; a room layout's answer names the room instead of the scene.

trash.description: <layouts dir name>/<scene>/.trash/<layout>-<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>[-n].json, or <layouts dir name>/@<room>/.trash/… for a room layout

render.description: v1 draws GLB only; splat is accepted and drawn as its GLB.

position.description: [x, elevation, z] in meters; elevation is the item's bottom above the floor, 0 to 4.

mounted.description: Kept from nook for old files; v1 never hangs on walls.

LayoutList.description: GET /api/layouts?scene=<name> (contract §2.7): the scene's layouts, sorted by name.

LayoutPut.description: PUT /api/layouts/<layout>?scene=<name> or ?room=<room> (contract §2.7, §4.9): a layout (layout.schema.json); the server sets name, scene_name or room_name (from the query; the other is dropped) and updated, and answers the stored layout. v1 also fills a missing uid (<id>-<n>), render (glb) and rotation_y_deg (0), so only id and position are required of an item.

title.description: The name as the user typed it; whitespace is collapsed, at most 120 characters after that (400 otherwise).
The name as the user typed it, or null.

LibraryAddAccepted.description: 202 of POST /api/library/items and POST /api/library/items/from-url (contract §2.8): the queued job and the engine's price (§3.2).

LibraryDeleted.description: DELETE /api/library/items/<id> (contract §2.8): the entry and its folder moved to library/.trash/<id>-<UTC stamp>/. v1 also says where (relative to the library).

LibraryFromUrl.description: POST /api/library/items/from-url (contract §2.8, §2.9 URL fetches): {image_url, ...meta}. The server downloads the image itself (http/https, public addresses only).

mount.description: v1 also takes null (the default, floor).

yaw.description: Degrees, around Y after the engine's default orientation (§3.1).

engine.description: An image engine: idol (default), sam3d, trellis2 or rug.

LibraryJob.description: A library job (contract §2.8 Jobs): GET /api/library/jobs/<id>, and inside the jobs list and the 202 answers. One queue, one job at a time, in memory.

kind.description: add: midstudy-add on an upload or a download; rescale: PATCH dims_cm or yaw (midstudy-add --rescale).

engine.description: The add's engine; v1 records glb for every rescale.

cost_usd.description: What it cost, once done (midstudy-add's summary); null until then and when it failed.

message.description: A status line; a failed job's is midstudy-add's stderr line; an upsert says it replaced the item.

LibraryJobs.description: GET /api/library/jobs (contract §2.8): every job since the server started, newest first.

LibraryListing.description: GET /api/library (contract §2.8): library.json (empty items when there's none) plus the trashed items, newest first.

LibraryMeta.description: An add's meta (contract §2.8): the JSON whose base64 is the X-Midstudy-Meta header of POST /api/library/items. Anything wrong is 400 with one actionable sentence.

mount.description: v1 also takes null (the default, floor).

yaw.description: Degrees, around Y after the engine's default orientation (§3.1).

engine.description: Images: idol (default), sam3d, trellis2 or rug. Models: glb (the only one; anything else is 400).

LibraryPatch.description: PATCH /api/library/items/<id> (contract §2.8): any of these. 200 the item, or 202 {job} when dims_cm or yaw changed (a rescale, $0). default_render must name an asset the item has, and an Idol piece can't show its stand-in box (400).

LibraryRescaleAccepted.description: 202 of PATCH /api/library/items/<id> when dims_cm or yaw changed (contract §2.8): the queued rescale job ($0).

LibraryTrash.description: library/.trash/<id>-<UTC stamp>/entry.json: the item's library entry as it was (its folder sits beside it).

LightAccepted.description: 202 of POST /api/scenes/<name>/light (contract §4.4, §4.8 backfill): the light job, or the same job again while one is queued or running.

LightDone.description: 200 of POST /api/scenes/<name>/light (contract §4.4) when the scene already has lighting.json: no job.

calib.description: Always null (a light job never calibrates).

lighting.description: true: lighting.json written; false: no clear light in the photo; null until it ran.

Lighting.description: Written by `midstudy-calib fit` (and `run`) next to calib.json. Units: three.js 0.180 light units, linear sRGB, for ACES Filmic at exposure 1. Frame: the camera's (three.js axes: x right, y up, z towards the viewer); the planner rotates it with the scene's current camera. Keys not listed here are allowed for diagnostics; readers ignore them.

source.description: photo: inferred from the photo; truth: the golden scenes' own lights (fixtures/scenes only).

image.description: photo.jpg's size when the fit ran.

camera.description: The camera block the fit used (informational: the planner uses the scene's current camera).

sh.description: L2 spherical harmonics, three.js SphericalHarmonics3 order [L00, L1-1 (y), L10 (z), L11 (x), L2-2, L2-1, L20, L21, L22], radiance coefficients as THREE.LightProbe takes them, camera frame, RGB. The key light is not included.

softness.description: 0 a hard sun edge, 1 very diffuse.

confidence.description: How clearly the photo shows one directional light.

Look.description: Applied to the furniture only, never to the photo (contract §4.5), and the lighting controls (contract §4.8). Every key is optional; a missing key takes its default.

contact_shadows.description: The soft dark patch under each piece on the floor (default true).

auto_light.description: Auto lighting (default true): the key light's direction and softness follow lighting.json, or the v1 key light without one.

light_azimuth_deg.description: Where the key light comes from, world frame, seen from above: 0 from straight ahead (-Z), 90 from the right (+X), ±180 from behind the camera. Used when auto_light is false.

light_elevation_deg.description: The key light's height above the horizon. Used when auto_light is false.

light_softness.description: Shadow softness, 0 hard to 1 very soft. Used when auto_light is false.

cast_shadows.description: The key light's shadow on the floor (default: on with lighting.json, off without).

LookPatch.description: Numbers are clamped to the ranges of scene.schema.json's look; null removes a key.

MemberScale.description: Multiplies the member scene's camera height_m to give its effective camera (contract §4.9); clamped to 0.25–4 by every writer.

PngDataUri.description: A PNG as a base64 data URI.

Pose.description: Where a member photo was taken, in the room frame (contract §4.9 Frames): its scene frame maps to the room frame by p_room = Ry(yaw) · p_scene + (x_m, 0, z_m). Every writer clamps x_m and z_m to −50…50 and brings yaw_deg into (−180, 180].

yaw_deg.description: Positive is counterclockwise seen from above (+X turns toward −Z), the sign of rotation_y_deg.

PosePut.description: A pose as the client sends it: any numbers (the server clamps x_m and z_m to −50…50 and brings yaw_deg into (−180, 180]).

PoseSource.description: origin: set when the room was created, on its first member (pose {0, 0, 0}); solver: from an align result; manual: the user moved or turned it (an align never overwrites it unless asked); unplaced: no pose (pose is null): just added, or the solver couldn't place it.

ProductError.description: A 4xx of POST /api/library/product (contract §2.11): one sentence; blocked: true when the shop refuses automatic reading (422).

ProductRequest.description: POST /api/library/product (contract §2.11): {url, llm?} for the server to read the page, or {html, url?, llm?} for a page the user's browser copied (then nothing is fetched). llm: false skips the language model.

url.description: The product page's link (http or https). v1 refuses one over 4096 characters (400).

html.description: The page's source, not blank; over 10 MB it is cut, with a warning.

ProductResult.description: 200 of POST /api/library/product (contract §2.11): what the product page says. It adds nothing. Every key is always present.

url.description: The page's final URL after redirects (a pasted page: the address it gives), without user:password@ or #fragment.

category.description: One plain word or two, or null.

dims_candidates.description: Every distinct size reading, best first.

variants.description: The shop's size options when it has more than one; the size the link names first.

images.description: The product's pictures (links only: the server never downloads them), product first.

source_layers_used.description: The layers that gave something, in this order; llm only when the model was called.

mock.description: True only when the model was called in mock mode.

dims_index.description: Index into dims_candidates; null when the label couldn't be read.

RenderList.description: GET /api/renders[?scene=<name>][&room=<room>] (contract §2.6, §4.7, §4.9): newest first; ?scene= keeps one photo's renders (with or without a room), ?room= keeps the renders made in that room.

mock.description: v1: whether the server runs with the fal mock (the contract is silent; the planner shows it).

RenderMeta.description: A render's metadata (contract §2.6, §4.7): the 200 answer of POST /api/render, what renders/<name>.json holds, and each entry of GET /api/renders.

input_url.description: The capture as sent (without its metadata).

raw_url.description: fal's output before keep-room's align; null without keep-room.

prompt.description: The prompt sent (the default one when none was given).

reference.description: The scene photo was sent as image 2 (nano-banana with a scene).

aligned.description: Keep-room's align result; null without keep-room.

out_w.description: The result's size; null when its frame header can't be read.

RenderRequest.description: POST /api/render (contract §2.6, §4.7). A model that isn't listed, an image that isn't a JPEG (or whose size can't be read) and keep_room without scene or mask are 400; an unknown scene is 404.

prompt.description: Replaces the default prompt when it isn't blank.

layout.description: The layout shown; a value that isn't a slug is recorded as null. With room, a room layout.

keep_room.description: Keep room exact (§4.7): needs scene and mask.

Room.description: rooms/<room>/room.json (contract §4.9): several scenes (photos of one room) in one shared frame, the room frame. Written by the server only: created by POST /api/rooms, changed by PUT /api/rooms/<room>, by an align job that finishes (§4.9 Align), by Set scale and by deleting or restoring a member scene. The folder name is the room's name; it never changes. Joining a room never rewrites a scene's scene.json.

name.description: room-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS (UTC of the POST), -2, -3… on collision; the folder name.

title.description: Free text (trimmed, at most 200 characters), or null (shows the date).

created.description: When the room was created, ISO-8601 UTC.

saved.description: The last change to anything but the title (members, poses, scales, an align result applied), ISO-8601 UTC; null until then.

members.description: The member scenes in order (the photo strip's order, numbered from 1). A scene is in at most one room. At most 32. May be empty (every member deleted); the room stays until it is deleted.

aligned.description: The last align result the server applied (§4.9 Align): which solver and when, or null when none was.

solver.description: Which solver answered: manhattan (the no-ML fallback), the chosen learned solver's name (e.g. vggt, mast3r, solv3r; Gate A, docs/ROOMS.md §5), truth (the golden room fixtures' mock answers), none (nothing could be placed: the mock without a match, or every solver failed).

finished.description: When the align job finished, ISO-8601 UTC.

RoomCreate.description: POST /api/rooms (contract §4.9): a new room of existing scenes, in this order. The first becomes the origin (pose {0, 0, 0}, pose_source origin), the others unplaced; every scale 1. Nothing is aligned until POST /api/rooms/<room>/align. 400 for a duplicate scene or a bad title, 404 for a scene that doesn't exist, 409 for a scene already in a room.

title.description: Trimmed; at most 200 characters after that (400 otherwise); blank or null means none.

RoomDeleted.description: 200 of DELETE /api/rooms/<room> (contract §4.9): the room's folder and layouts/@<room>/ moved to rooms/.trash/<room>-<UTC stamp>; its scenes stay where they are, in no room.

RoomDetail.description: GET /api/rooms/<room>, and the answer of POST /api/rooms (201) and PUT /api/rooms/<room> (200) (contract §4.9): room.json, each member with its scene object, its scene's camera and its effective camera, align.json (or null), and the alignment's status.

title.description: Free text (trimmed, at most 200 characters), or null (shows the date).

aligned.description: The last align result the server applied (§4.9 Align): which solver and when, or null when none was.

layouts.description: How many room layouts it has (layouts/@<room>/).

align.description: rooms/<room>/align.json as it is (the solver's last answer), or null without one (or when it can't be read).

align_error.description: The failed align job's sentence, else null.

RoomJobs.description: GET /api/rooms/jobs (contract §4.9): align jobs, newest first. They run on the calibration queue but are listed here, not in GET /api/scenes/jobs.

RoomList.description: GET /api/rooms (contract §4.9): the rooms newest first (by created, ties by the name's collision suffix as a number, as scenes), and the deleted rooms newest first.

RoomMember.description: One member photo. pose is null exactly when pose_source is unplaced.

RoomMemberDetail.description: A member (room.json), its scene object, the camera its scene.json uses and its effective camera: that camera with height_m × scale, clamped to 0.2–3.0 (contract §4.9).

RoomMemberObject.description: A member (room.json) and its scene object (§4.4).

pose.description: Numbers are clamped and yaw brought into (−180, 180].

RoomObject.description: The room object (contract §4.9): each entry of GET /api/rooms, and the answer of POST /api/rooms/<room>/restore. room.json's fields, each member with its scene object, the number of room layouts and the alignment's status. GET /api/rooms/<room> carries more (room-detail).

title.description: Free text (trimmed, at most 200 characters), or null (shows the date).

aligned.description: The last align result the server applied (§4.9 Align): which solver and when, or null when none was.

layouts.description: How many room layouts it has (layouts/@<room>/).

align_error.description: The failed align job's sentence, else null.

RoomPut.description: PUT /api/rooms/<room> (contract §4.9 Changes): any of title, members, reset and rescale, applied in that order. Numbers are clamped (pose and scale ranges of room.schema.json); unknown keys or bad values are 400, an unknown scene 404, a scene in another room 409, reset without align.json 409. Answers the room (room-detail).

title.description: Trimmed; at most 200 characters after that (400 otherwise); blank or null removes it.

members.description: The whole new member list, in order: a scene not listed leaves the room (its pose is forgotten), a new one joins (unplaced, scale 1, unless it carries a pose), the order is the new order. Per entry, a pose that differs from the stored one is stored with pose_source manual (null makes it unplaced); a scale is stored as given (clamped), its pose_source unchanged.

reset.description: Align photos' Reset: these members go back to align.json's answer, re-expressed in the room frame as an align result is applied (§4.9 Align), with pose_source solver (unplaced when align.json doesn't place them); an origin member is left as it is. Members not in the room are 400.

rescale.description: The room's Set scale: multiplies every member's scale and every pose's x_m and z_m by this factor (then clamps); pose_source is unchanged; layouts are not rewritten (as a scene's Set scale).

RoomTrash.description: rooms/.trash/<room>-<UTC stamp>/trash.json (contract §4.9): room.json and align.json sit beside it, the room's layouts in layouts/ inside it.

Scene.description: Written by the server: created when the upload is accepted, updated by PUT /api/scenes/<name> and by a calibration that finishes while camera_source is auto or default. The folder name is the scene's name; it never changes.

title.description: Free text, set on upload (X-Midstudy-Meta) or by rename; null shows the date.

created.description: When the upload was accepted, ISO-8601 UTC.

saved.description: Last PUT that changed more than the title, ISO-8601 UTC; null until then.

camera_source.description: auto: copied from calib.json; manual: the user changed it in Adjust floor; default: no calibration yet, or it failed.

SceneCreated.description: 202 of POST /api/scenes (contract §4.4): the queued calibration (run) and the new scene's name. The scene exists (and is listed, calib_status pending) from this moment.

SceneDeleted.description: 200 of DELETE /api/scenes/<name> (contract §4.4): the folder and layouts/<name>/ moved to scenes/.trash/<name>-<UTC stamp> (v1 names the scenes folder as it is called: scenes by default).

SceneDetail.description: GET /api/scenes/<name> and the 200 of PUT /api/scenes/<name> (contract §4.4, §4.8): scene.json, the scene object's fields, calib (public), lighting and the light's status.

title.description: Free text, or null (shows the date).

photo_url.description: Null until photo.jpg exists; may carry a ?v=<mtime> cache buster.

layouts.description: How many layouts the scene has.

calib_status.description: pending while a job is queued, running while it runs, else done when calib.json exists and the last job (if any) succeeded, else failed (also a calibration lost to a restart).

calib_error.description: The failed calibration's sentence, else null.

room.description: The room the scene is a member of, or null (contract §4.9). Optional in the schema so that a server without rooms conforms; a server with rooms always sends it.

calib.description: calib.json without exif.make and exif.model, or null.

lighting.description: lighting.json as it is, or null without one.

lighting_status.description: done with lighting.json; else the newest light job's pending, running, failed or none (it found no light), unless a newer calibration decides (pending, running); else missing.

lighting_error.description: A failed light job's sentence, else null.

SceneJob.description: A job of the calibration queue (contract §4.4, §4.8 backfill): a calibration (c-…) or a light job (l-…). GET /api/scenes/jobs/<id>, and inside the jobs list and the 202 answers. In memory: a restart forgets them.

SceneJobs.description: GET /api/scenes/jobs (contract §4.4): calibration and light jobs, newest first.

SceneList.description: GET /api/scenes (contract §4.4): the scenes newest first (by created, ties by the name's collision suffix as a number), and the deleted scenes newest first.

SceneMeta.description: The optional X-Midstudy-Meta header of POST /api/scenes (contract §4.4): base64 of this JSON. title is trimmed, at most 200 characters (400 otherwise).

SceneObject.description: The scene object (contract §4.4, §4.9): each entry of GET /api/scenes, and the answer of POST /api/scenes/<name>/restore. GET /api/scenes/<name> carries the same fields (scene-detail).

title.description: Free text, or null (shows the date).

photo_url.description: Null until photo.jpg exists; may carry a ?v=<mtime> cache buster.

layouts.description: How many layouts the scene has.

calib_status.description: pending while a job is queued, running while it runs, else done when calib.json exists and the last job (if any) succeeded, else failed (also a calibration lost to a restart).

calib_error.description: The failed calibration's sentence, else null.

room.description: The room the scene is a member of, or null (contract §4.9). Optional in the schema so that a server without rooms conforms; a server with rooms always sends it.

ScenePut.description: PUT /api/scenes/<name> (contract §4.4, §4.8): any of title, camera, camera_source, look. Camera values and look numbers are clamped (so any number is accepted); a look replaces only the keys it carries and a key set to null is removed. Unknown keys or wrong types are 400. saved is stamped unless only title changed.

title.description: Trimmed; at most 200 characters after that (400 otherwise); blank is null.

SceneThumbSaved.description: 200 of PUT /api/scenes/<name>/thumb (contract §4.4): thumb.jpg written without metadata.

SceneTrash.description: scenes/.trash/<name>-<UTC stamp>/trash.json. A folder trashed before this file existed is read from its name instead.

SceneTrashRoom.description: Present when the scene was a member of a room when it was deleted (contract §4.9): the room, the member's 0-based index in members and its member record. Restoring the scene puts it back into that room at min(index, number of members) with this record, when the room exists (not in the trash) and the scene isn't in another room; otherwise the scene comes back on its own.

Settings.description: GET and PUT /api/settings (contract §2.9 Settings): the daily fal budget, its default and maximum, and whether the server's --daily-spend-usd fixes it.

locked.description: true: --daily-spend-usd fixes the budget and PUT is 409.

SettingsPut.description: PUT /api/settings (contract §2.9 Settings): the daily fal budget in USD, 0 to 10000, saved rounded to cents in <library>/settings.json; 400 out of range, 409 while --daily-spend-usd fixes it.

Spend.description: GET /api/spend (contract §2.9): today's (UTC) spend from costs.csv, what running calls have reserved, and the cap.

SpendRefused.description: 402 over the daily spend cap (contract §2.9): no call was made. Also the answer for a call that costs more than the whole cap.

ThumbPut.description: PUT /api/scenes/<name>/thumb and PUT /api/library/items/<id>/thumb (contract §2.6, §2.8, §4.4): a JPEG of at most 2 MB (413 over it, 400 when it isn't a JPEG). It is stored without its metadata.

Upload.description: What was uploaded (set by the server; informational): the original file name, its extension (source.<ext>) and size.
